A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gated in-context/in-weight learning framework. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic classification and Omniglot experiments in Section 3 and Appendix B, plus Gemini Nano fine-tuning outcomes in Section 4 and Tables 2–3.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds stylized-model and GRU experiments in Appendix B.2 and extended-training results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The gated mixture and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 adds an experimental neural variant of the stylized model: Euclidean-distance context prediction and two-layer, 64-unit ReLU networks for the IW predictor and selector, extending the original tabular formulation.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic classification, Omniglot, and the Gemini name–city task, including IBD/OOBD and heldout-image evaluations. Always-relevant contexts already appear in v1's IC-predictor experiments. V2's additional architectures and longer runs extend evaluation within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated GRU alternative in Appendix B.2 and Figure 15. Its context-length sweep also displays IW and IC comparator results in Figure 11, whereas v1 Figure 6 reports transformer-only OOBD errors. Existing transformer comparisons and the Gemini base-model comparator remain.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces additional experiments with N = 10^7, zero input noise, always-relevant contexts, and millions of gradient updates on synthetic data and Omniglot. This substantially extends the evaluation horizon. Appendix B.2 also introduces controlled architecture substitutions; these are additional protocols, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 newly examines the stylized model's actual predictor errors and selector probabilities under noise, context-length, and class-cardinality variations, and tests robustness across architectures using a GRU. Appendix D adds extended-training analyses of persistence when both IC and IW prediction can solve the task.

E5.justification: The stated five-seed synthetic experiments, three-seed Omniglot experiments, and one-standard-deviation reporting practice are retained. The added architecture plots also report five seeds. No new statistical testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced, and Figure 21 does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds selector-probability and predictor-error curves, GRU results, and detailed context-length results. Figure 21 newly shows persistent synthetic ICL and partially retained Omniglot ICL after millions of updates under its added protocol. The retained Figure 2 is described as showing similar rather than lower IW error. Gemini Tables 2–3 retain their predictions and numerical values.

T1.justification: V2 adds cross-entropy-specific Krichevsky–Trofimov upper/lower excess-risk rate claims of order log(Nx)/Nx, continuous-input extension assumptions in Appendix A.1, and a label-noise derivation comparing IW error p with IC error 2p(1−p) in Appendix D. V1's generalization proposition is retained in Appendix A; the main regret results and proofs largely remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central gated-selection and memorization claims remain. The introduction now qualifies its explanation of transience by requiring asymptotically better IW prediction, explicitly leaves the equal-performance case unresolved, and identifies persistent or coexisting IC/IW behavior as a contribution. The abstract and conclusion largely retain their previous claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D substantially expands the explanation and limitations of transience, discussing task difficulty, finite-time performance, mixed training data, selector smoothness, and label-noise correlation. It explicitly acknowledges that IC-trained transformers may implement IWL, complicating measurement, and that equal-optimal-performance cases remain unresolved. Appendix B.2 additionally discusses applicability beyond transformers.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly specifies the stylized model's distance calculation, 64-unit ReLU networks, and a single-layer GRU with hidden size 64, including token sequencing and output processing. These provide concrete implementation information for the added experiments. Existing transformer specifications and Gemini training prompts are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Lin and Lee, Panwar et al., Chung et al., and sources supporting the additional theory. It also explicitly contrasts the Gemini experiment with Wei et al. and qualifies its relationship to Singh et al.'s transience findings. Reddy's year correction and merged duplicate references do not represent new research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 edits selected contribution, related-work, and experimental-result passages; moves the generalization proposition into Appendix A; and expands the appendix organization with a short Section 3.3 pointer. The overall introduction–theory–experiments–LLM–conclusion sequence and much of the existing method and proof prose remain.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout, redraws Figure 1 with IW lower/upper bounds and different axes, and substantially reorganizes the main experimental figures. It adds the data-generation schematic and architecture/extended-training plots, while relocating retained material such as v1 Figure 8 to v2 Figure 18. The Gemini tables are reformatted without changing their entries.

improvement.justification: V2 supplements v1's transformer-proxy evidence with direct selector analyses, GRU tests, and extended-training experiments, while more clearly qualifying its explanation of transience. These improve empirical support and claim calibration, although equal-performance dynamics remain unresolved. The new Figure 6 caption also reverses the IW/IC training descriptions stated in Section 3.1. The net quality gain is positive but limited.
